tour.name: North Bali Private Tour: Jatiluwih Rice Terraces, Ulun Danu Bratan Lake Temple & Waterfalls

tour.overview:
The centre of Bali is a highland of old volcanic craters filled with lakes, cool forests and terraced rice fields, at more than 1,000 metres above sea level. The lakes are sacred as the source of the water that irrigates the island's rice through the subak system, and the temple of Ulun Danu Bratan honours Dewi Danu, the goddess of the lake. Jatiluwih, on the slopes of Mount Batukaru, has the most extensive rice terraces in Bali and is part of the island's UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape.

This private day takes you through the highlands with a licensed guide and a car. You walk through the rice terraces of Jatiluwih, visit the lake temple, look down on the twin lakes and swim beneath a waterfall in the jungle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bali
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; walks in the rice fields and steps down to the waterfall

WHAT YOU SEE
• Jatiluwih rice terraces.
• Ulun Danu Bratan temple.
• Candikuning market.
• The Handara gate.
• The twin lakes viewpoint.
• Banyumala or Gitgit waterfall.

WHY THIS WORKS
The highlands are far from the south coast and poorly served by public transport; with a car, you see the terraces, lakes and waterfalls in one comfortable day.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, walkers, photographers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer the culture of Ubud, choose our Ubud tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The highlands are much cooler than the coast and often misty in the afternoon: bring a light jacket. The waterfall paths are steep and slippery. The rice is green from about January to March and July to September, and golden before harvest.

days.name: Jatiluwih rice terraces, Ulun Danu Bratan, the Handara gate, the twin lakes and a jungle waterfall
days.description:
What to expect: the cool highlands of Bali, with a licensed guide, private car, entrance fees and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 7:30 and drive north through villages and forest, about two hours, to Jatiluwih on the slopes of Mount Batukaru. You walk along the narrow dykes and trails between the terraces, which spread across the valley for more than 600 hectares. Your guide explains how the farmers of a subak share water through canals controlled from small temples, how red rice, a local variety, is grown here, and the rituals that accompany each stage of the crop. Lunch is at a restaurant overlooking the terraces.

You continue up to Lake Bratan, a crater lake at 1,200 metres, where the temple of Ulun Danu Bratan, built in 1633, stands on small islands near the shore, so that its eleven-tiered and three-tiered meru towers seem to float on the water, often with the mountains wrapped in mist behind. You stop at the Candikuning market, full of highland fruit, strawberries, spices and orchids, and at the Handara gate, a split temple gate framing the forested hills.

From a ridge viewpoint you look down on the twin lakes of Buyan and Tamblingan, surrounded by jungle. You end at a waterfall, Banyumala or Gitgit depending on the season and conditions, where a path through the forest leads down to cascades falling into a natural pool, where you can swim. You are back at your hotel at about 17:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:30 – Jatiluwih rice terraces walk.
11:30 – Lunch with a view.
13:00 – Ulun Danu Bratan temple.
14:00 – Candikuning market and Handara gate.
14:45 – Twin lakes viewpoint.
15:15 – Waterfall and swim.
17:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A stay in the north-coast town of Lovina, with dolphin watching at dawn, can be added.
• Waterfall paths are steep; wear shoes with grip.
• In the rainy season some waterfalls close for safety.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance fees, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About two hours from the south coast to the highlands, and about the same back.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes: Jatiluwih, Ulun Danu Bratan and the waterfall.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, with a view of the rice terraces. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Can we swim at the waterfall?
faq.answer: Yes, when conditions allow. Bring a swimsuit and towel.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the rice fields, the fruit market and the waterfall. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Ulun Danu Bratan has flat gardens; the rice-field walk and waterfall path are uneven and steep.

faq.question: Is it cold in the highlands?
faq.answer: It is cool, around 18 to 24 °C, and can be misty. Bring a light jacket.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Bali but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with grip, a light jacket, swimwear and covering clothes for the temple.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October for dry weather. The rice terraces are greenest in the months after planting.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
